# Importing CSD and MIDI

Importing replaces the active project with a new Blue project. Save work in
the current project before starting an import, then save the imported result
as a `.blue` file. Open a project first; the import commands are disabled
when no project is loaded. The original source file remains separate.

## Import a CSD

Choose **File → Import CSD File** and select a `.csd`. Blue asks where the
`CsScore` events should go:

| Choice                          | Result                                                                 |
| ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Global Score**                | Places imported score text in the [Global Score](globals.qmd).         |
| **Single Sound Object**         | Creates GenericScore material, splitting score sections where present. |
| **Sound Object per Instrument** | Splits each section again by instrument.                               |

Blue parses orchestra instruments and UDOs, global orchestra text, settings,
tables, and supported score statements. The score importer handles `f`, `i`,
`s`, and valid `t` tempo statements; it is not a general Csound score parser.
After import, inspect **Project → Generate CSD to Screen**, instrument IDs,
table references, and media paths before rendering. See
[GenericScore](generic-score.qmd) and [Tables](tables.qmd).

## Import a MIDI file

Choose **File → Import MIDI File** and select a MIDI file. The **MIDI Import
Settings** dialog shows streams with note data, grouped by source track and
channel. Each row shows its note range and lets you set an **Instrument ID**,
**Note template**, and **Trim** choice. The instrument ID and template must
be nonempty; instrument ID zero is rejected.

The default template is:

```text
i<INSTR_ID> <START> <DUR> <KEY> <VELOCITY>
```

Expand **Template placeholders** in the dialog for the full list, including
`<KEY_PCH>`, `<KEY_OCT>`, `<KEY_CPS>`, and `<VELOCITY_AMP>`. Adapt the template
to the target Csound instrument's `p` fields. **Trim** removes leading
silence within that stream: the layer starts at its first note and the
first generated note is written at beat zero. Review imported layers and
timing before replacing the source MIDI file in your workflow.

## Add an audio file

For an audio recording that should play as recorded, add an **AudioClip** to
an audio Track in the [Score](score.qmd). A Track can route it through the
[Mixer](mixer.qmd). For a file-driven SoundObject with its own playback
instrument and post code, use [AudioFile](audio-file.qmd) instead. Set the
project's [Media Folder](project-properties.qmd) before importing if the
project should copy its audio into a portable folder.
